title: Plan each component with at most 5 methods; split it when more are needed

facts.note: Planner authoring, revising or reviewing a plan, wagon or component spec; the harness needs a phase observer to know planning is in progress.
Planner artifacts that declare components and their methods are identifiable by file kind/path.

Source has implementation type none; a counter of declared methods per component must be built. Fires on any planned component over the cap, regardless of whether its method list changed in this edit.

fires: Planner declares a new component with 6 or more methods
Planner adds a method to an existing component that already has 5 methods
Planner revises or reviews an artifact containing an existing component with more than 5 methods, even if its method list is unchanged (e.g. only its description is edited)
Planner reduces a component from 9 methods to 6 — still over the cap
doesNotFire: A planned component declares 5 or fewer methods
Planner edits the description of a component that already has 5 or fewer methods
Artifacts that do not declare components (e.g. acceptance wording only)

given: A plan, wagon or component spec you are authoring, revising or reviewing declares a component and its methods (new or existing)
when: You plan or review any component, whatever the edit — adding, removing or leaving its methods unchanged
then: Keep every component at 5 methods or fewer; if the capability needs more methods, split it into several focused components instead of exceeding the cap.
prefer: Split an over-full component along business-capability lines so each resulting component owns one capability with ≤ 5 methods
Keep a component small and focused, e.g. a validator with 3 methods (validate, eligibility check, explain)
avoid: A single component with 9 (or any > 5) methods — split it into focused components
Leaving an existing over-limit component as-is, or trimming it to a count still above 5 (e.g. 9 → 6), and treating that as compliant
Gaming the cap by merging distinct operations into one catch-all method or moving methods into an unnamed helper bag instead of splitting by capability
why: Capping a component at 5 methods keeps it focused on a single business capability; exceeding it signals the component is doing too much and should be split.
evidence: Count the methods declared for each component in the plan/spec (new and existing); every count is ≤ 5
Where a capability needed more than 5 methods, the plan shows it split into multiple focused components
verifier_detail: Term max_methods (label 'Maximum methods per component'): max_methods = 5; condition is method count ≤ 5 (6+ is a finding); applies to every declared component, not only ones whose method list changed
Term action: 'Split component if more methods needed'
Source example (compliant): 'OptionValidator with 3 methods: validate, isEligible, explain'
Source counter-example: 'A component with 9 methods — split into focused components'
No automated implementation exists (implementation.type: none); detection must count declared methods per component
